voices.note: transmits Rav Nachman's ruling (91a.4) and poses the three dilemmas (91a.5-6)
anonymous Gemara voice: פשיטא, מהו דתימא ... קמשמע לן

props.gloss_en: Rav Nachman: one who carried out a dried-fig bulk for eating and reconsidered it for sowing, or for sowing and reconsidered it for eating, is liable
[what the ruling teaches:] liability for carrying out does not require the lifting and the placing to be under one intention
Rava's dilemma: one carried out half a dried fig for sowing, it swelled, and he reconsidered it for eating -- is he liable?
Rava: and if you say [in the first dilemma that he is liable] -- one carried out a dried-fig bulk for eating, it shrank, and he reconsidered it for sowing -- is he liable?
Rava: and if you say we go by now and he is liable -- one carried out a dried-fig bulk for eating, it shrank and swelled again -- is he liable?
Rava: is there dichui (permanent disqualification once the measure lapsed) with regard to Shabbat, or is there not?

questions.gloss_en: Rava: half a fig for sowing that swelled, reconsidered for eating -- unlike Rav Nachman's case (there, either way there is a measure), here at the time he carried it out there was no eating measure, so not liable; or perhaps, since had he stayed silent he would be liable on the sowing intention, now too he is liable? -- never resolved (the chain ends תיקו)

Rava: [presupposing dilemma 1 resolves 'liable'] a fig for eating that shrank, reconsidered for sowing -- here, had he stayed silent, on the first intention he is not liable; or perhaps we go by now and he is liable? -- never resolved (the chain ends תיקו)
Rava: [presupposing dilemma 2 resolves 'we go by now'] a fig for eating that shrank and swelled again -- is there dichui for Shabbat or not? -- תיקו
